newsitem.title: SPAIN: SPANISH INVESTMENT ABROAD UP 16 PERCENT IN H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: SPANISH INVESTMENT ABROAD UP 16 PERCENT IN H1 1997.

text.p: Total Spanish investments abroad in the first half of 1997 rose to 535.20 billion pesetas, up 16 percent versus the same period last year, the Economy Ministry said on Thursday.
Latin America was the principal destination of Spanish investments, representing 61 percent of the total or 325.74 billion pesetas compared to 34 percent in the first half of 1996.
Brazil was the top recipient with 22 percent, followed by Venezuela, 18 percent and Argentina, 14 percent.
The increase in investment in Latin America came at the expense of the European Union, other OECD countries and tax havens.
Investment in the European Union fell to 21 percent of the total compared to 32 percent in the same period last year.
Within the European Union, investments were heaviest in Portugal, seven percent of the total, followed by the Netherlands and Luxembourg, four percent, and the United Kingdom, two percent.
Within OECD countries, only investments in the United States were up to seven percent of the total.
